Clopidogrel may also be used for purposes not listed in this medication guide.

You should not use clopidogrel if you have any active bleeding such as a stomach ulcer or bleeding in the brain.
Clopidogrel increases your risk of bleeding, which can be severe or life-threatening.
Call your doctor or seek emergency medical attention if you have bleeding that will not stop.
Call your doctor or seek emergency medical attention if you have blood in your urine.
Call your doctor or seek emergency medical attention if you have black or bloody stools.
Call your doctor or seek emergency medical attention if you cough up blood or vomit that looks like coffee grounds.
Do not stop taking clopidogrel without first talking to your doctor, even if you have signs of bleeding.
Stopping clopidogrel may increase your risk of a heart attack or stroke.

chunks.text:
You should not use clopidogrel if you are allergic to clopidogrel, or if you have:
any active bleeding; or
a stomach ulcer or bleeding in the brain (such as from a head injury).
Tell your doctor if you have ever had:
an ulcer in your stomach or intestines; or
a bleeding disorder or blood clotting disorder.
Clopidogrel may not work as well.
This may happen if you have certain genetic factors.
These genetic factors affect the breakdown of this medicine in your body.
Your doctor may perform a blood test to make sure clopidogrel is right for you.
This medicine is not expected to harm an unborn baby.
However, taking clopidogrel within 1 week before childbirth can cause bleeding in the mother.
Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant.
You should not breastfeed while using this medicine.

chunks.text:
Follow all directions on your prescription label and read all medication guides or instruction sheets.
Use these medicines exactly as directed.
Clopidogrel can be taken with or without food.
Clopidogrel is sometimes taken together with aspirin.
Take aspirin only if your doctor tells you to.
Clopidogrel keeps your blood from coagulating (clotting).
It can make it easier for you to bleed, even from a minor injury.
Contact your doctor or seek emergency medical attention if you have any bleeding that will not stop.
You may need to stop using clopidogrel for a short time before a surgery, medical procedure, or dental work.
Any healthcare provider who treats you should know that you are taking clopidogrel.
Do not stop taking clopidogrel without first talking to your doctor, even if you have signs of bleeding.
Stopping the medicine could increase your risk of a heart attack or stroke.
Store at room temperature away from moisture and heat.

Unstable Angina (UA)/Non-ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (NSTEMI) has a loading dose of 300 mg orally once.
The maintenance dose is 75 mg orally once a day.
The duration of therapy is optimal unknown.
ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI) has an optional loading dose of 300 mg orally once.
The maintenance dose is 75 mg orally once a day, with or without thrombolytics.
The optimal duration of therapy is unknown.
Comments: -Administer Clopidogrel in combination with aspirin 75 mg to 325 mg orally once a day.
The benefit of Clopidogrel is unknown.
This applies to patients who undergo primary percutaneous coronary intervention.
Uses include prevention of atherothrombotic events.
This applies to patients with non-ST-segment elevation acute coronary syndrome.
This includes patients with UA.
This includes patients with NSTEMI.

chunks.section_heading: What should I avoid while taking clopidogrel?
chunks.text:
Avoid alcohol.
Alcohol can increase your risk of stomach bleeding.
Avoid activities that may increase your risk of bleeding or injury.
Use extra care to prevent bleeding while shaving or brushing your teeth.
If you also take aspirin.
Ask a doctor or pharmacist.
Do this before using medicines for pain, fever, swelling, or cold/flu symptoms.
They may contain ingredients similar to aspirin.
These ingredients include salicylates, ibuprofen, ketoprofen, or naproxen.
Taking these products together can increase your risk of bleeding.

chunks.section_heading: What other drugs will affect clopidogrel?
chunks.text:
Sometimes it is not safe to use certain medications at the same time.
Some drugs can affect your blood levels of other drugs you take.
This may increase side effects.
This may make the medications less effective.
Tell your doctor about all your other medicines, especially:
a stomach acid reducer such as omeprazole, Nexium, or Prilosec;
an antidepressant such as citalopram, fluoxetine, sertraline, Cymbalta, Effexor, Lexapro, Pristiq, or Prozac;
rifampin;
a blood thinner --warfarin, Coumadin, Jantoven; or
NSAIDs (nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs) --aspirin, ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin), naproxen (Aleve), celecoxib, diclofenac, indomethacin, meloxicam, and others.
This list is not complete.
Other drugs may affect clopidogrel.
These other drugs include prescription and over-the-counter medicines.
These other drugs also include vitamins and herbal products.
Not all possible drug interactions are listed here.
